title: Samut Songkhram in 1 Day: Maeklong, Amphawa, Fireflies | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A one-day Samut Songkhram trip from Bangkok: the train at Maeklong Railway Market, grilled prawns at Amphawa Floating Market, and a night firefly boat. Hours, prices and honest tips.
keywords: Samut Songkhram one day trip, Maeklong Railway Market, Amphawa Floating Market, firefly boat tour, Mae Klong day trip from Bangkok
intro: Samut Songkhram sits just over an hour from Bangkok, but there's enough to fill a full day without staying overnight. In the morning you watch a train squeeze through the Maeklong Railway Market, in the afternoon you stop by a riverside temple, in the evening you eat your way through Amphawa Floating Market, and you close the night with a boat ride to see fireflies in the dark. This is a one-day plan we've paced so it actually fits — no rushing until you're worn out.

blocks.html: The most worthwhile one-day Samut Songkhram trip is on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday, because Amphawa Floating Market and the firefly boats only run on those three days (plus public holidays). The Maeklong Railway Market, on the other hand, is open daily. Come on a weekday and you'll only get the railway market and the temples, but you'll miss Amphawa in the evening — so lock in the day before you set off.

blocks.text: The one-day plan, morning to night

blocks.html: Leave Bangkok around 7am and drive down Rama II Road; about an hour and a half later you're in Mae Klong. We've timed it to catch a mid-morning train slot at the railway market, then work our way toward Amphawa through the afternoon and evening.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Maeklong Railway Market — watch the train cut through

items.activity: Leave Bangkok, drive down Rama II Road toward Mae Klong
items.note: Around 70–75 km, about 1.5 hours; allow extra for morning traffic

items.activity: Arrive at the railway market, park and walk into the market on the tracks
items.note: There's a parking lot near Mae Klong Station; parking runs about 20–40 THB

items.activity: Walk the market and wait to see the vendors pull in their awnings and stalls as the train comes
items.note: Train slots are roughly 08:30, 09:00, 11:10 and 11:30 — double-check the timetable board at the station on the day you go

items.activity: Sample the market food — old-style coffee, fruit, fresh seafood
items.note: This is a real wet market; Mae Klong seafood is fresher and cheaper than in the city

blocks.title: Tip about the train
blocks.html: The train times do shift a little in practice, so don't stand right up against the edge of the tracks. Wait for the vendors to start folding their awnings, then step all the way back and keep a firm grip on your phone. The train moves slowly, but the carriages are wide enough to nearly brush the goods on both sides.

items.activity: Lunch around Mae Klong — fish noodles or a riverside seafood spot
items.note: The short, hook-faced Mae Klong mackerel is a local specialty; order a plate of fried mackerel

items.activity: Drive to Wat Bang Kung to see the ordination hall wrapped entirely in the roots of a huge tree
items.note: Open roughly 08:00–16:30; stop by Bang Kung Camp and photograph the stucco fighting roosters too

items.activity: Sit at a canalside cafe near Amphawa and rest your eyes before the market opens
items.note: The Amphawa area has several cafes in old wooden houses, good for ducking out of the afternoon sun

blocks.label: Evening–night
blocks.title: Amphawa Floating Market + firefly boat ride

items.activity: Walk Amphawa Floating Market, which gets lively around 4pm
items.note: The boat stalls start opening around 16:00 and run until about 10pm, Friday–Sunday only

items.activity: Eat along the canal — grilled river prawns, fried oysters, boat noodles, Thai sweets
items.note: Grab a seat by the water and order straight from the boats; grilled prawns are the dish people come to Amphawa for

items.activity: Book a spot on a firefly boat at the pier by the district office or a pier in the market
items.note: A shared boat is about 60–80 THB per person, or charter the whole boat; the ride takes about 1 hour

items.activity: Cruise out to watch fireflies blinking in the Lamphu trees along the Mae Klong River
items.note: Fireflies are most plentiful in the rainy season (May–Oct), and you'll see them clearest on a moonless night

items.activity: Head back to keep walking the market, grab some souvenirs and drive back to Bangkok
items.note: You'll be home a little after 10pm — a proper morning-out, evening-back day trip

blocks.title: What to know about the fireflies before you get your hopes up
blocks.html: Fireflies are a natural thing — some nights there are loads, some nights only a few, depending on rain, the tide and the moonlight. On a bright, full-moon night, or where there are lots of lights along the bank, you'll see fewer of them. If you really want a good show, pick a moonless night in the rainy season for better odds — and don't shine a flash at them, it disturbs the fireflies.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't miss on this trip

blocks.html: Samut Songkhram is a genuine food town — Mae Klong seafood, old-school Thai sweets and grilled dishes along the Amphawa canal. Here are the dishes we think are most worth it if you've only got a single day.

items.name: Grilled river prawns
items.blurb: Amphawa's signature dish — big prawns grilled over charcoal by the canal, dipped in a sharp seafood sauce. Plenty of people come to Amphawa for this one plate alone.
items.meta: Evening–night at Amphawa · priced by prawn size

items.name: Fried Mae Klong mackerel
items.blurb: Short, hook-faced mackerel with rich, tender flesh — a local specialty of the province. Eat it with shrimp-paste chili dip and fresh vegetables at lunch.

items.name: Fried oysters & stir-fried razor clams
items.blurb: Fresh seafood from Don Hoi Lot — fried oysters that are crisp outside and soft inside keep you going, while the spicy stir-fried razor clams suit the riverside mood.

items.name: Boat noodles
items.blurb: Small bowls with a deep, rich broth, ordered from a boat that pulls up to the bank — a floating-market image you have to try at least one bowl of.
items.meta: Evening at Amphawa · from a few tens of THB a bowl

items.name: Canalside Thai sweets
items.blurb: Khanom sai sai, banana sweets, thong yip and thong yot, khanom krok — lots of vendors to choose from all along the walkway, great to snack on or take home.

items.name: Old-style coffee at the railway market
items.blurb: In the morning, after the train excitement, drop into an old-style coffee shop in the market for an oliang or hot coffee and watch the easygoing rhythm of the wet market.

blocks.text: If you have time to spare, where else to stop

items.name: King Rama II Memorial Park
items.blurb: A museum of Thai-style houses and a garden of plants from classic Thai literature, right next to Amphawa — good for an afternoon stop before the market opens.

items.name: Don Hoi Lot
items.blurb: A mudflat at the mouth of the Mae Klong River with seafood restaurants and souvenir stalls — good if you start the trip early and want a seafood lunch.

items.name: Tha Kha Floating Market
items.blurb: A low-key, local-style floating market that's still not crowded, open on certain days by schedule — good for those who like quiet corners the crowds haven't reached.

items: Private car — from Bangkok take Rama II Road, about 70–75 km; the most convenient option for this plan since you'll be hopping between several spots
Van/coach — there are services from the Southern Bus Terminal (Sai Tai Mai) to Mae Klong, then a songthaew or motorbike taxi on to Amphawa
Parking — the railway market has a lot near the station; Amphawa gets busy with cars in the evening, so it's best to park in a lot outside the market and walk in
Which day to go — Friday–Sunday, so you get both Amphawa Floating Market and the firefly boats

faq.q: Which day should you visit Samut Songkhram for a one-day trip?
faq.a: If you want the full set — the Maeklong Railway Market, Amphawa Floating Market and a firefly boat ride — you need to go on a Friday, Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, because Amphawa Floating Market and the firefly boats only run on those three days. The railway market is open daily.

faq.q: What time does the train pass through Maeklong Railway Market?
faq.a: The train passes through the market about 8 times a day. The rough times are 06:20, 08:30, 09:00, 11:10, 11:30, 14:30, 15:30 and 17:40. Times can shift a little, so check the timetable board at Mae Klong Station again on the day you go.

faq.q: How much is the Amphawa firefly boat ride?
faq.a: A shared boat is around 60–80 THB per person and takes about 1 hour, or you can charter the whole boat. You can arrange it at the piers in front of the Amphawa district office and in the market, or through your hotel or homestay.

faq.q: When is the best time to see the most fireflies?
faq.a: Fireflies are most plentiful in the rainy season, roughly May to October, and you'll see them clearest on a moonless night, since moonlight and lights along the bank make them harder to spot. It's nature, so some nights there are many and some nights few.

faq.q: Is one day enough, or should you stay overnight?
faq.a: A morning-out, evening-back day trip works fine, since it's only about an hour and a half from Bangkok. But if you want to take it easier and skip the late-night drive home, staying a night by the water in Amphawa adds a quiet canalside morning to your trip too.
